key_insight: Electron beam welding can successfully reconstitute Charpy impact specimens for RPV steels, producing dense weld zones with no obvious cracking and mostly preserved mechanical performance.
engineering_relevance: This suggests EBW is a viable specimen-reconstitution route for nuclear materials testing, supporting safer and more practical evaluation of reactor pressure vessel steels.
method: Reconstituted Charpy impact specimens of 16MND5, 10Cr12Ni3Mo2VN, and X6NiCrTiMoVB 25-15-2 using electron beam welding.
Characterized weld-zone microstructure with optical microscopy and scanning electron microscopy.
Assessed quality through non-destructive flaw detection, Vickers hardness, and impact toughness testing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports dense weld-zone microstructure, no obvious crack defects, and the best overall match to original specimens for 10Cr12Ni3Mo2VN.
watch_item: Results are based on a small set of steel grades and specimen-scale testing, so broader process robustness and full-service performance still need validation.
paper_title: Effects of electron beam welding on the microstructure and impact properties of three reconstituted steels
